title: Winning $100 in the tiger-in-your-tank game
summary: Riddick tells at length how he scratched off a gas-station card and won $100, then tells of meeting William Bendix at Blaise D'Antoni's party.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Oh, this is when I won $100 for a tiger in your tank. Oh, yeah.
I won Tiger Reno. Yeah. Souvenir, huh? Well, I'm glad to know you. I've never known anybody who won any of those games.

It was the funniest thing in the world. And I was down in St. Bernard. I'd been on a call. And I had a brand new car, a Plymouth. And they claimed that if you were out on the road during the first 500 miles, and it came up to 500 miles to add a quart of oil to your car until you could get back to your own filling station, then have your oil changed. So, I said to myself, I looked at my speedometer, and it says 500 miles. I said, well, I'll stop at the first name filling station I come to, and it happened to be standard, you know, Esso. The man put the quart of oil, just added the quart of oil to my engine. And, uh, says, uh, handed me this little soap of paper. He said, here, this might do you some good. He said, when you get a chance, he said, just scratch off that, uh, uh, smutty-like marking on there, and see what it says. You may win something. I never gave it another thought. I put it in my pocket, my coat pocket. Three times on the way to town, I reached in my pocket, and I felt for this thing. I was smoking at the time, smoking cigarettes. And, uh, I saw this card, and I started to throw it away, and something stopped me. I put it back in my pocket. I waited until I got back at Whirline, five o'clock that afternoon. This happened before lunch. The man gave it to me. And I took it out and looked at it, and it said, scrape off that little gray marking on there. So I took my fingernail like that and scraped it off. And it says, winner of $100. Myra Mendel. Doc Sushan. Mildred. Scoop Kennedy. Who this lady is, I don't remember. And Alec Templeton. So, I don't know what these things are. These are some of that RTE, Sacred Breaker Corporation things. Roosevelt Review. William Bendix. Yeah. Played a party for Blaze D'Antonio on Just On Piano. And Bendix was there. He was a personal friend of Bendix. And Blaze introduced me to Bendix. And Bendix says, I like the way you play. He says, what did you say your name was? I said, Riddick. He says, I'll be damned. He says, there was a Riddick once from Indianapolis. I said, that's my oldest brother. He said, a friend of ours, a mutual friend of our...
